profiles.meeting_scenario: An economic advisory firm is coordinating a client-ready briefing for a regional banking roundtable on inflation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The meeting is between the lead economist who owns the analytical workstream and the policy operations manager who owns packaging and circulation across the client-facing workstream. Agenda: confirm what will be handed off by Thursday, which data cut will be used for the exchange-rate and money-supply visuals, what 'sign-off' is needed before sending materials to the country office, and how the shared briefing files will be updated. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the Thursday handoff, the numbers to use, and the approval path for distributing the materials.

members.name: David Ilunga
members.expertise: Inflation modeling, VAR analysis, central bank policy, Francophone African economies
members.background: David trained as a monetary economist and previously worked on central-bank technical assistance projects in Central Africa; he leads the analytical workstream for the DRC inflation-indicators study and is most comfortable working from research memos and model output tables.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve the analytical nuance of the original study and avoid last-minute presentation rework; he is also trying to protect time for a separate client model update due the same week.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'briefing pack,' they usually mean the economist's note plus appendix tables, because the deck can be assembled from that afterward.
Using the 'latest numbers' means the latest fully cleaned monthly series in the research workbook, not a newer but unharmonized dashboard extract.
Once the senior economist has checked the narrative and the numbers, the material is effectively 'signed off' for circulation within the project team.
Updating the shared file means replacing charts and tables in the existing working deck directly from his analysis folder rather than rebuilding them in a different presentation format.

members.name: Sarah Bennett
members.expertise: Cross-team coordination, executive briefings, stakeholder circulation, document control
members.background: Sarah has spent years managing donor and policy-facing deliverables for economic consulting projects; she translates technical outputs into roundtable-ready materials and manages approval workflows across country and regional teams.
members.private_state: She needs something client-presentable by Thursday afternoon and wants to avoid a repeat of a previous incident where a technically correct draft was circulated before country leadership had cleared it.
hidden_assumptions: The 'briefing pack' for any external-facing event normally means a polished slide deck with a short executive note, because senior stakeholders rarely read technical appendices.
The 'latest numbers' are whatever appears in the current treasury/dashboard reporting cycle, since external stakeholders expect the most recent month even if methodology notes are still pending.
'Sign-off' includes country director and communications clearance whenever a file may leave the core project team, even if it is still labeled as draft.
Updating the shared file means putting content into the controlled client-facing folder using the standard branded PowerPoint template with bilingual labels and source notes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to finalize the 'briefing pack' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: David means a research note summarizing the inflation-indicator findings, plus appendix tables and rough charts that Sarah can later convert into presentation materials.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Sarah means the actual roundtable-ready package: a polished 8-10 slide deck and a two-page executive summary suitable for immediate circulation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In their organization, both teams routinely use the phrase 'briefing pack,' and each hears a familiar workflow implied by it; because both assume the other understands the normal handoff from their own function, neither asks what files are included.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the exchange-rate chart should use the 'latest numbers.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: David is thinking of the March monthly-average BCC-aligned exchange-rate series in the econometrics workbook, which is the latest cleaned series matched to the model and variance decomposition.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Sarah is thinking of the April end-of-month exchange-rate figure in the treasury dashboard, which is the latest month shown in all current external briefing materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe there is one obvious 'latest' series and neither expects that the other is using a different reporting object; because the phrase sounds routine and operational, it does not trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the pack should be 'signed off' before it goes out.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: David believes sign-off is achieved once the senior economist confirms the interpretation of exchange rate, money supply, and public consumption and the numbers reconcile with the model outputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Sarah believes sign-off requires country director approval and communications clearance before anything is sent beyond the immediate working group, even as a draft.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same project-management term and sincerely endorse the need for review, but each applies the approval standard typical of their own workflow; the divergence hides behind a shared commitment to quality control.

misalignment_points.topic: How the shared file will be 'updated'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that David will 'update the deck' and Sarah will pick it up afterward.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: David plans to overwrite charts in the internal working deck stored in the research team's SharePoint folder, leaving formatting and source-note clean-up for later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Sarah expects David to update the controlled client-facing PowerPoint in the delivery folder, using the standard template structure so she can circulate it immediately after minimal checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The sentence describes a familiar handoff and sounds sufficiently specific to both of them, yet the file location, template, and level of polish are treated as obvious background details rather than decision points.
